paragraphs.title: Courage in the Face of a Powerful Enemy

easy.question: What did Israel see when going out to battle?
answers: Horses, chariots, and a large army
A great river
Angels in heaven
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel would see horses, chariots, and a people more numerous than they were.

easy.question: Who approached the people and spoke to them before the battle?
answers: The king
The priest
The army commander
easy.explanation: When the people came near the battle, the priest approached them and spoke.

easy.question: What were the people commanded to do in the face of the enemy?
answers: Run away immediately
Hide
Not be afraid
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly command the people not to be afraid or terrified.

medium.question: Why should Israel not fear the enemy, even though it has horses, chariots, and a large army?
answers: Because the Lord their God goes with them
Because the enemy is small in number
Because there is no real battle
medium.explanation: The reason is that the Lord is with Israel and fights for them.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verses?
answers: The priest speaks, and then the people go to battle
The people approach the battle, and then the priest approaches and speaks
The people win, and then the priest blesses them
medium.explanation: First they approach the battle; then the priest approaches the people and speaks.

medium.question: In the phrase “do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them,” what response is forbidden?
answers: Gathering the enemy
Moving away from the enemy
Being frightened and losing courage before the enemy
medium.explanation: The context shows that the people are commanded not to tremble or become terrified before the enemy.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast in the first verse?
answers: The enemy appears strong and numerous, but Israel is commanded not to fear
Israel is small in number, but the enemy runs away
The people cannot see the enemy, but the priest can
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the enemy’s outward strength but emphasizes that Israel should not fear because the Lord is present.

challenge.question: Why are the Israelites reminded that the Lord brought them out of Egypt?
answers: To teach the exact route of the exodus
To remind them that the Lord has saved them in the past
To compare Egypt with the enemy’s number of soldiers
challenge.explanation: The Exodus is a reminder of the Lord’s past help and strengthens confidence in his help during the battle.

challenge.question: What is the exact order of the warnings in the priest’s speech?
answers: Do not fear, do not let your hearts faint, do not tremble, do not be terrified
Do not be terrified, do not tremble, do not fear, do not let your hearts faint
Do not let your hearts faint, do not fear, do not be terrified, do not tremble
challenge.explanation: The verse lists them in this order: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, and do not be terrified.

questions.question: What is the main contrast in the first verse?
answers: The enemy appears strong and numerous, but Israel is commanded not to fear
Israel is small in number, but the enemy runs away
The people cannot see the enemy, but the priest can
questions.explanation: The verse presents the enemy’s outward strength but emphasizes that Israel should not fear because the Lord is present.

questions.question: Why are the Israelites reminded that the Lord brought them out of Egypt?
answers: To teach the exact route of the exodus
To remind them that the Lord has saved them in the past
To compare Egypt with the enemy’s number of soldiers
questions.explanation: The Exodus is a reminder of the Lord’s past help and strengthens confidence in his help during the battle.

questions.question: What is the exact order of the warnings in the priest’s speech?
answers: Do not fear, do not let your hearts faint, do not tremble, do not be terrified
Do not be terrified, do not tremble, do not fear, do not let your hearts faint
Do not let your hearts faint, do not fear, do not be terrified, do not tremble
questions.explanation: The verse lists them in this order: let not your hearts faint, fear not, do not tremble, and do not be terrified.

paragraphs.title: Exemptions from Battle and Strengthening the Heart

easy.question: Who told the people who was allowed to return home?
answers: The officers
The army commanders
The priests
easy.explanation: The verses say that the officers spoke to the people and announced who could return home.

easy.question: What should a man do if he has built a new house but has not dedicated it?
answers: Remain in the camp
Return home
Give the house to the army
easy.explanation: A man who has built a new house but has not dedicated it is told to go and return home.

easy.question: Who is allowed to return home according to verse 8?
answers: A man who has planted a vineyard
A man who is betrothed
A man who is fearful and fainthearted
easy.explanation: The verse says that the fearful and fainthearted man should return home.

medium.question: In what order are the first three personal situations mentioned?
answers: A new house, a vineyard, a betrothed wife
A vineyard, a new house, fear
A betrothed wife, a vineyard, a new house
medium.explanation: The text first mentions a man who built a house, then one who planted a vineyard, and finally one who is betrothed.

medium.question: Why may a man who built a house or planted a vineyard return home?
answers: Because he is not required to serve in the army
So that he will not die in battle and another man will enjoy his work
Because he must train the soldiers
medium.explanation: In each case, the stated reason is that he might die in battle and another person would dedicate his house or enjoy the fruit of his labor.

medium.question: In the phrase “lest his brethren’s heart faint as well as his heart,” what effect is being warned against?
answers: Strengthening the others
Praising the others
Weakening or frightening the others
medium.explanation: The fearful man is not to weaken the courage of his fellow soldiers through his own fear.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the first three men and the fearful, fainthearted man?
answers: The first three have unfinished personal matters, while the last may affect the morale of his fellow soldiers
The first three are not soldiers, while the last is an army commander
The first three return because they are wealthy, while the last returns because of his age
challenge.explanation: The first three fear leaving behind an undedicated house, an uneaten vineyard, or an unconsummated marriage; the fearful man may discourage his fellow soldiers.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the officers speak first and the army commanders organize the people afterward?
answers: The army commanders choose who will build houses
Those who are exempt are removed from the army first, and the soldiers are organized afterward
The officers conduct the battle instead of the army commanders
challenge.explanation: The exemptions are announced first; afterward, the army commanders arrange the remaining forces.

challenge.question: What repeated detail emphasizes that each of the first three situations is unfinished?
answers: Each man has already completed his personal matter
Each man is afraid of the battle
In each case, the final action has not yet occurred: dedicating the house, eating from the vineyard, or taking the wife
challenge.explanation: The house has not been dedicated, the vineyard has not yet been enjoyed, and the betrothed woman has not yet been taken as a wife.

questions.question: What is the main difference between the first three men and the fearful, fainthearted man?
answers: The first three have unfinished personal matters, while the last may affect the morale of his fellow soldiers
The first three are not soldiers, while the last is an army commander
The first three return because they are wealthy, while the last returns because of his age
questions.explanation: The first three fear leaving behind an undedicated house, an uneaten vineyard, or an unconsummated marriage; the fearful man may discourage his fellow soldiers.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the officers speak first and the army commanders organize the people afterward?
answers: The army commanders choose who will build houses
Those who are exempt are removed from the army first, and the soldiers are organized afterward
The officers conduct the battle instead of the army commanders
questions.explanation: The exemptions are announced first; afterward, the army commanders arrange the remaining forces.

questions.question: What repeated detail emphasizes that each of the first three situations is unfinished?
answers: Each man has already completed his personal matter
Each man is afraid of the battle
In each case, the final action has not yet occurred: dedicating the house, eating from the vineyard, or taking the wife
questions.explanation: The house has not been dedicated, the vineyard has not yet been enjoyed, and the betrothed woman has not yet been taken as a wife.

easy.question: What was Israel commanded to do when approaching a city to fight it?
answers: Proclaim peace to it
Surround it immediately
Leave the area
easy.explanation: The verse commands Israel to proclaim peace to the city before fighting.

easy.question: What would happen if the city answered with peace and opened its gates?
answers: Israel would return to its land
The people of the city would become tributaries and serve Israel
The city would remain completely independent
easy.explanation: If the city agrees to peace and opens its gates, its people become tributaries and serve Israel.

easy.question: What should Israel do if the city refuses peace and makes war?
answers: Send it gifts
Ask it for help
Besiege it
easy.explanation: If the city does not make peace and fights against Israel, Israel is commanded to besiege it.

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Proclaim peace, receive a response, and then fight if the city refuses
Fight, proclaim peace, and then open the gates
Besiege the city, leave, and then negotiate
medium.explanation: First peace is proclaimed; if the city agrees, it becomes tributary, but if it refuses and fights, it is besieged.

medium.question: Why is it important whether the city opens its gates?
answers: It shows whether Israel can enter without resistance
It determines who will be king of Israel
It shows whether the city is in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Opening the gates expresses acceptance of the peace terms, while refusal and war lead to a siege.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee,” what does becoming tributaries mean?
answers: Becoming snow
Becoming subject to required service or payment
Receiving complete peace with no conditions
medium.explanation: The phrase describes people who owe service or payment to the ruling power; the verse adds that they will serve Israel.

challenge.question: What distinction between the city’s two possible responses appears in the verses?
answers: Accepting peace leads to servitude, while refusing peace leads to war and a siege
Accepting peace leads to destruction, while refusing peace leads to independence
The city remains unchanged in both cases
challenge.explanation: The verses present two different outcomes: agreement brings tribute and service, while refusal and war bring a siege.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that peace is offered before the siege?
answers: The city must open its gates immediately
The city is given an opportunity to avoid battle by agreeing to the terms
Israel is forbidden to fight any city
challenge.explanation: The offer of peace gives the city a choice of agreement instead of conflict, although the agreement includes tribute and service.

challenge.question: Which wording emphasizes that the city’s negative response turns the situation into a military conflict?
answers: The words “peace” and “open”
The words “all the people” and “found therein”
The words “will make no peace” and “will make war against thee”
challenge.explanation: These expressions explicitly describe the change from rejecting peace to making war, followed by the siege.

questions.question: What distinction between the city’s two possible responses appears in the verses?
answers: Accepting peace leads to servitude, while refusing peace leads to war and a siege
Accepting peace leads to destruction, while refusing peace leads to independence
The city remains unchanged in both cases
questions.explanation: The verses present two different outcomes: agreement brings tribute and service, while refusal and war bring a siege.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that peace is offered before the siege?
answers: The city must open its gates immediately
The city is given an opportunity to avoid battle by agreeing to the terms
Israel is forbidden to fight any city
questions.explanation: The offer of peace gives the city a choice of agreement instead of conflict, although the agreement includes tribute and service.

questions.question: Which wording emphasizes that the city’s negative response turns the situation into a military conflict?
answers: The words “peace” and “open”
The words “all the people” and “found therein”
The words “will make no peace” and “will make war against thee”
questions.explanation: These expressions explicitly describe the change from rejecting peace to making war, followed by the siege.

paragraphs.title: Conquering a Distant City and Taking the Spoil

easy.question: Who delivers the city into Israel’s hands?
answers: The Lord thy God
The king of the city
The enemy army
easy.explanation: The verse says, “when the Lord thy God hath delivered it into thine hands.”

easy.question: Who was Israel commanded to smite with the sword?
answers: The women
Every male
The animals
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword.”

easy.question: What may Israel take from the city?
answers: Only its weapons
Only its houses
All its spoil
easy.explanation: The verse allows Israel to take all the spoil of the city, including the people and possessions listed.

medium.question: What order is described after the city is delivered into Israel’s hands?
answers: The males are killed, and the rest is taken as spoil
The spoil is burned, and then the males are killed
The women and children are sent away, and then the spoil is taken
medium.explanation: First the males are struck down; afterward, the women, children, cattle, and all the spoil are taken.

medium.question: In the phrase “all the spoil thereof, shalt thou take unto thyself,” what does “spoil” mean?
answers: Protecting the city
Taking the goods and possessions captured in war
Leaving immediately
medium.explanation: Spoil means the possessions captured from an enemy, as the verse explains by referring to the spoil of the enemies.

medium.question: Which cities are described as being treated this way in verse 15?
answers: All the cities of every nation without exception
Only cities within the land of Israel
Distant cities that are not cities of those nations
medium.explanation: The verse limits this instruction to distant cities that are not among the cities of the listed nations.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the distinction between “the cities which are very far off” and “the cities of these nations”?
answers: The verse distinguishes two groups of cities and does not give the same instruction for all of them
All the cities are in the same location
The distant cities are not enemy cities
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies a particular category of distant cities and excludes the cities of the listed nations from it.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the spoil is not limited to objects?
answers: The mention of the sword
The mention of women, children, and cattle
The mention of distant cities
challenge.explanation: The verse includes people and animals among the spoil, not only inanimate possessions.

challenge.question: What condition limits the phrase “all the cities which are very far off”?
answers: The cities must be small
They must be near the sea
They must not be among the cities of those nations
challenge.explanation: The phrase is qualified by the condition that the cities must not belong to the listed nations.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the distinction between “the cities which are very far off” and “the cities of these nations”?
answers: The verse distinguishes two groups of cities and does not give the same instruction for all of them
All the cities are in the same location
The distant cities are not enemy cities
questions.explanation: The verse identifies a particular category of distant cities and excludes the cities of the listed nations from it.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the spoil is not limited to objects?
answers: The mention of the sword
The mention of women, children, and cattle
The mention of distant cities
questions.explanation: The verse includes people and animals among the spoil, not only inanimate possessions.

questions.question: What condition limits the phrase “all the cities which are very far off”?
answers: The cities must be small
They must be near the sea
They must not be among the cities of those nations
questions.explanation: The phrase is qualified by the condition that the cities must not belong to the listed nations.

paragraphs.title: The Law Concerning the Cities of the Inhabitants of the Land

easy.question: What was Israel forbidden to do to every living thing in these nations’ cities?
answers: Let it live
Teach it
Settle it
easy.explanation: The verse says, “thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth.”

easy.question: Who gives these nations’ cities to Israel as an inheritance?
answers: The king of Israel
The Lord thy God
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord thy God gives these cities to Israel for an inheritance.

easy.question: Which people are not mentioned in the list of nations in verse 17?
answers: The Hittites
The Egyptians
The Jebusites
easy.explanation: The Hittites and Jebusites are mentioned, but the Egyptians are not.

medium.question: Why was Israel commanded to destroy these nations?
answers: So that they would not teach Israel their abominations
To increase Israel’s army
To teach them the law
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the purpose was to prevent these nations from teaching Israel to practice their abominations.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt utterly destroy them,” what action is commanded?
answers: Blessing them
Destroying them completely
Inviting them to peace
medium.explanation: The phrase means complete destruction, as confirmed by the command to spare nothing that breathes.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the command in verse 17 and the purpose in verse 18?
answers: The command is the result of learning the abominations
The command is intended to prevent Israel from learning the abominations
The command is intended to teach the nations new customs
medium.explanation: Verse 18 explains that destroying the nations is intended to prevent them from influencing Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word “that” at the beginning of “That they teach you not”?
answers: It introduces the purpose of the command
It gives the name of one of the nations
It indicates that the command has already been carried out
challenge.explanation: The phrase introduces the purpose: preventing the nations from influencing Israel.

challenge.question: Who might learn the nations’ abominations according to verse 18?
answers: The nations’ gods
The Israelites
The nations that have already been destroyed
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the nations might teach “you,” meaning the Israelites.

challenge.question: What behavior of the nations is described as a danger to Israel?
answers: Their abominable practices before their gods
Their trade with Israel
Their wars among themselves
challenge.explanation: The verse warns against learning all the abominations that these nations practiced before their gods, which could lead Israel into sin.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the word “that” at the beginning of “That they teach you not”?
answers: It introduces the purpose of the command
It gives the name of one of the nations
It indicates that the command has already been carried out
questions.explanation: The phrase introduces the purpose: preventing the nations from influencing Israel.

questions.question: Who might learn the nations’ abominations according to verse 18?
answers: The nations’ gods
The Israelites

questions.explanation: The verse says that the nations might teach “you,” meaning the Israelites.

answers: Their abominable practices before their gods

Their wars among themselves
questions.explanation: The verse warns against learning all the abominations that these nations practiced before their gods, which could lead Israel into sin.

paragraphs.title: Protecting Fruit Trees During a Siege

easy.question: What must not be destroyed during a siege?
answers: A fruit tree
The city wall
Weapons
easy.explanation: The verse forbids destroying a tree from which people eat.

easy.question: According to the verse, what may people eat from?
answers: The city wall
The tree
The axe
easy.explanation: The verse says, “for thou mayest eat of them,” referring to the trees.

easy.question: What may be done to a tree that is not a fruit tree?
answers: Only water it
Only protect it
Destroy and cut it down
easy.explanation: A tree that does not provide food may be cut down and used for the siege.

medium.question: Why must a fruit tree not be cut down during a war?
answers: Because people can eat from it
Because it is too tall
Because it belongs to the city
medium.explanation: The stated reason is that the tree provides food: “for thou mayest eat of them.”

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Eating, cutting down every tree, and leaving the city
Besieging the city, distinguishing between types of trees, and using non-fruit trees
Building a city, planting trees, and ending the war
medium.explanation: First the city is besieged; then fruit trees are distinguished from other trees, and only permitted trees are used.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt build bulwarks against the city,” what does building bulwarks mean?
answers: Building a road to the city
Planting trees around the city
Building siege works around the city to bring it under control
medium.explanation: The wartime context shows that bulwarks are siege structures used to pressure the city until it is subdued.

challenge.question: What important distinction is made between the trees?
answers: Between tall trees and short trees
Between fruit trees and trees that are not fruit trees
Between trees in the city and trees in the countryside
challenge.explanation: The verse permits cutting only trees known not to be fruit trees.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the words “until it be subdued”?
answers: The siege continues until the city is conquered or brought under control
The army immediately retreats
The trees grow again
challenge.explanation: The words describe continuing the siege until the city is subdued.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast between a fruit tree and a non-fruit tree in these verses?
answers: The first may not be cut down, while the second may be cut down for the siege
The first is used for the siege, while the second is used only for food
The first belongs to the enemy, while the second belongs to Israel
challenge.explanation: Fruit trees are preserved because they provide food, while non-fruit trees may be used to build the siege works.

questions.question: What important distinction is made between the trees?
answers: Between tall trees and short trees
Between fruit trees and trees that are not fruit trees
Between trees in the city and trees in the countryside
questions.explanation: The verse permits cutting only trees known not to be fruit trees.

questions.question: What can be learned from the words “until it be subdued”?
answers: The siege continues until the city is conquered or brought under control
The army immediately retreats
The trees grow again
questions.explanation: The words describe continuing the siege until the city is subdued.

questions.question: What is the main contrast between a fruit tree and a non-fruit tree in these verses?
answers: The first may not be cut down, while the second may be cut down for the siege
The first is used for the siege, while the second is used only for food
The first belongs to the enemy, while the second belongs to Israel
questions.explanation: Fruit trees are preserved because they provide food, while non-fruit trees may be used to build the siege works.
